what: SpaceX launches massive Starship V3 rocket on test flight

clean_source_blocks.text: Elon Musk's SpaceX has launched the biggest-ever Starship rocket a day after its highly anticipated test flight was delayed. The uncrewed Starship V3 rocket blasted off from its launchpad in Texas just after 17:30 (2230 GMT) on Friday, days after SpaceX revealed plans for a record-breaking stock market debut. The test flight ended after about an hour later when Starship splashed down into the Indian Ocean and exploded as planned. "Congratulations @SpaceX team on an epic first Starship V3 launch & landing!" Musk posted on his X platform. "You scored a goal for humanity." The first attempted launch on Thursday was postponed due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin in the launch tower.

Update: SpaceX scrubbed a Starship flight test May 21 due to what CEO Elon Musksaid on X was an issue with the "hydraulic pin holding the tower arm in place" not retracting. Another launch attempt is scheduled for Friday, May 22, with a window opening at 6:30 p.m. ET. SpaceX's mammoth Starship rocket could be getting off the ground for the first time in 2026 in just a matter of hours. Seven months have elapsed since billionaire Elon Musk's commercial spaceflight company last launched the world's largest rocket from South Texas. Since that October test flight, SpaceX teams have been working to prepare a next-generation version of Starship for its highly-anticipated debut.
The first attempted launch on Thursday was postponed due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin in the launch tower.

SpaceX has launched the 12th test flight of its massive Starship spacecraft. Elon Musk’s aerospace company launched Starship during ‌a 90-minute ⁠launch window which opens at 5.30pm Central Time (11.30pm BST). SpaceX was within 30 seconds of launching the test flight a day earlier when it called off the launch after a number of problems arose with the brand-new pad at Starbase, near the Mexican border. Musk has hailed the launch as 'epic' and a 'goal for humanity' - while cheers and chants of 'USA, USA' rang out across SpaceX headquarters. While the liftoff itself went well, not all of the engines fired as the booster attempted a controlled return.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Elon Musk's SpaceX has launched the biggest-ever Starship rocket a day after its highly anticipated test flight was delayed.

The uncrewed Starship V3 rocket blasted off from its launchpad in Texas just after 17:30 (2230 GMT) on Friday, days after SpaceX revealed plans for a record-breaking stock market debut.

The test flight ended after about an hour later when Starship splashed down into the Indian Ocean and exploded as planned. "Congratulations @SpaceX team on an epic first Starship V3 launch & landing!" Musk posted on his X platform. "You scored a goal for humanity."

The first attempted launch on Thursday was postponed due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin in the launch tower.

The SpaceX team celebrated after the launch of the most powerful and tallest rocket ever, and while the mission achieved most of its major objectives, it did not go exactly to plan.

SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said the booster failed to complete its so-called boost-back burn after launch.

One of Starship's engines also malfunctioned, which forced a slightly longer burn from the remaining five to compensate. While it did not fly into exactly the correct orbit, Huot said it was travelling along a trajectory that was "within bounds".

"I wouldn't call it nominal orbital insertion," Huot said.

Nasa Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and the SpaceX team.

"One step closer to the Moon… one step closer to Mars," he posted on X.

During its suborbital cruise phase, Starship successfully released its payload of 20 mock Starlink satellites, along with two satellites that scanned its heat shield and sent data back to the ground during the its descent.

It was the 12th flight of a SpaceX rocket, and this time featured its latest design which stands 124 meters (407 feet) high.

The debut of the Starship V3 comes ahead of SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO), which is set to be the largest in Wall Street history. It could start next month.

Because of the shares Musk will own in SpaceX, which values itself at $1.25tn, the listing could make him the first-ever trillionaire.

SpaceX not only makes rockets, but has a satellite internet service called Starlink, and owns the controversial artificial intelligence (AI) firm xAI.

SpaceX was within 30 seconds of launching the test flight a day earlier when it called off the launch after a number of problems arose with the brand-new pad at Starbase, near the Mexican border.

Musk has hailed the launch as 'epic' and a 'goal for humanity' - while cheers and chants of 'USA, USA' rang out across SpaceX headquarters.

While the liftoff itself went well, not all of the engines fired as the booster attempted a controlled return.

The spacecraft also had to make do with fewer engines, but kept heading eastward 120 miles (194 kilometers) up. A pair of modified, camera-equipped Starlinks ejected from Starship provided brief views of the spacecraft in flight — a remarkable first.

The spacecraft reached its final destination — the Indian Ocean — despite some engine trouble, before erupting in flames upon impact. That last part was not unexpected, according to SpaceX.

Musk called it “an epic” launch and landing.

“You scored a goal for humanity,” he told his team via X.

Elon Musk has announced an IPO for SpaceX(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

SpaceX is celebrating what they believe is a very special day having successfully carried out their latest test.

As landings go, this one was pretty dramatic.

As it hurtled from the sky at ridiculously high speeds, it came down as planned and scheduled - but with a massive bang. A huge plume of smoke and fireball filled the air as it crashed back to earth for the first time.

payload.title: SpaceX laukaisi Starship V3 -raketin koelennolle Texasista
payload.summary: SpaceX on laukaissut miehittämättömän Starship V3 -raketin koelennolle Texasista sen jälkeen, kun edellinen yritys oli keskeytetty laukaisutornin hydrauliikkaongelman vuoksi.
payload.content:
SpaceX on laukaissut miehittämättömän Starship V3 -raketin koelennolle Texasista päivä sen jälkeen, kun odotettu lähtö oli peruttu laukaisutornin teknisen vian vuoksi. Lähteiden mukaan raketti nousi alustaltaan perjantaina hieman kello 17.30 jälkeen paikallista aikaa, ja lento päättyi noin tunnin kuluttua Intian valtamereen suunnitellulla alasroiskahduksella ja räjähdyksellä.

## Koelento seurasi keskeytettyä yritystä

Torstain laukaisuyritys keskeytettiin aivan viime vaiheessa, koska laukaisutornissa havaittiin ongelma hydrauliikkatapissa, jonka oli määrä vetäytyä pois tornivarren lukituksesta. Ongelma esti lennon toteuttamisen tuolloin, ja seuraava yritys siirrettiin perjantaille.

Starship V3 on kuvattu SpaceX:n seuraavan sukupolven versiona yhtiön suuresta Starship-järjestelmästä. Kyseessä oli miehittämätön koelento, jonka tarkoituksena oli testata raketin ja siihen liittyvän laukaisujärjestelmän toimintaa todellisessa lentoprofiilissa. Yhtiö on valmistellut uutta versiota useiden kuukausien ajan edellisen Starship-lennon jälkeen.

## Lento päättyi suunniteltuun mereenlaskeutumiseen

Koelento kesti noin tunnin. Starship päätyi Intian valtamereen ja räjähti lähdetietojen mukaan suunnitellulla tavalla. Tällaisissa koelennossa tavoitteena ei ole välttämättä ehjän aluksen talteenotto, vaan järjestelmän eri vaiheiden testaaminen ja mittausdatan kerääminen tulevia lentoja varten.

Laukaisun alkuvaiheen kerrottiin sujuneen hyvin, mutta kaikista yksityiskohdista ei ole vielä kattavaa teknistä arviota. Yhden lähteen mukaan kaikki moottorit eivät toimineet suunnitellusti kantoraketin yrittäessä hallittua paluuta. Tätä tietoa ei paketissa vahvisteta yksityiskohtaisella SpaceX:n teknisellä raportilla, joten sen merkitys lennon kokonaisarvioon jää vielä avoimeksi.

## Musk juhli onnistunutta testiä

SpaceX:n perustaja Elon Musk kommentoi laukaisua X-palvelussa ja onnitteli yhtiön tiimiä ensimmäisestä Starship V3 -lennosta ja laskeutumisesta. Hän kuvaili suoritusta ihmiskunnan kannalta merkittäväksi hetkeksi.

Koelento tapahtui samaan aikaan, kun SpaceX:ään kohdistuu laajaa huomiota myös yhtiön tulevaisuuden rahoitussuunnitelmien vuoksi. Varsinainen uutistapahtuma on kuitenkin tekninen: Starship V3 saatiin ilmaan lykätyn yrityksen jälkeen, ja lento vietiin läpi noin tunnin mittaisena testinä.
summary_bullets: SpaceX laukaisi miehittämättömän Starship V3 -raketin Texasista perjantaina.
Torstain yritys keskeytettiin laukaisutornin hydrauliikkaongelman vuoksi.
Noin tunnin mittainen koelento päättyi Intian valtamereen suunnitellulla alasroiskahduksella ja räjähdyksellä.

Elon Musk's SpaceX has launched the biggest-ever Starship rocket a day after its highly anticipated test flight was delayed. The uncrewed Starship V3 rocket blasted off from its launchpad in Texas just after 17:30 (2230 GMT) on Friday, days after SpaceX revealed plans for a record-breaking stock market debut. The test flight ended after about an hour later when Starship splashed down into the Indian Ocean and exploded as planned. "Congratulations @SpaceX team on an epic first Starship V3 launch & landing!" Musk posted on his X platform. "You scored a goal for humanity." The first attempted launch on Thursday was postponed due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin in the launch tower.

Update: SpaceX scrubbed a Starship flight test May 21 due to what CEO Elon Musksaid on X was an issue with the "hydraulic pin holding the tower arm in place" not retracting. Another launch attempt is scheduled for Friday, May 22, with a window opening at 6:30 p.m. ET. SpaceX's mammoth Starship rocket could be getting off the ground for the first time in 2026 in just a matter of hours. Seven months have elapsed since billionaire Elon Musk's commercial spaceflight company last launched the world's largest rocket from South Texas. Since that October test flight, SpaceX teams have been working to prepare a next-generation version of Starship for its highly-anticipated debut.

The first attempted launch on Thursday was postponed due to a malfunctioning hydraulic pin in the launch tower.

SpaceX has launched the 12th test flight of its massive Starship spacecraft. Elon Musk’s aerospace company launched Starship during ‌a 90-minute ⁠launch window which opens at 5.30pm Central Time (11.30pm BST). SpaceX was within 30 seconds of launching the test flight a day earlier when it called off the launch after a number of problems arose with the brand-new pad at Starbase, near the Mexican border. Musk has hailed the launch as 'epic' and a 'goal for humanity' - while cheers and chants of 'USA, USA' rang out across SpaceX headquarters. While the liftoff itself went well, not all of the engines fired as the booster attempted a controlled return.
